source: Client CSV 2026-10-14 (segmentation by product/technology, service/business model, application, end user, geography); cap 120, one browser per market, global search with the focus countries first
market_definition: The Global Precision Agriculture & Agricultural Drone Market covers companies making and supplying the following. Products and technology: Drone type: spraying drone, mapping/scouting drone, seeding drone, hybrid drone; hardware: flight controller, navigation/positioning module, imaging sensor, spray system; software: NDVI analytics, prescription maps, farm-management integration. Services and business models: Drone sale, drone-as-a-service, spraying-as-a-service, data-analytics subscription, training and support, managed farm-intelligence program. Applications: Crop monitoring, precision spraying, field mapping, crop scouting, seeding, fertilizer/nutrient application, irrigation planning, yield estimation, insurance and damage assessment. End users: Individual farmers, farmer-producer organizations/cooperatives, agricultural service providers, agribusinesses, plantations, research institutions, government agencies. Geography: Asia-Pacific, North America, Europe, Latin America, Middle East & Africa; India, Brazil, U.S., China, and Southeast Asia as key country markets.
core_scope: A core player itself makes and sells agricultural drones under its own name (spraying, mapping / scouting, seeding or hybrid drones and their spray systems, flight controllers and imaging payloads) or delivers drone-based precision agriculture under its own name: spraying-as-a-service, drone-as-a-service, NDVI / prescription-map analytics and managed farm-intelligence programmes. Diversified drone or agri-tech companies with an agricultural drone line qualify.
adjacent_segments: Tractor-mounted or ground precision-ag equipment makers with no drone
Farm-management software with no drone data
Drone distributors and dealers of other brands
scope: ONLY companies that operate in this market under their own name. A core player itself makes and sells agricultural drones under its own name (spraying, mapping / scouting, seeding or hybrid drones and their spray systems, flight controllers and imaging payloads) or delivers drone-based precision agriculture under its own name: spraying-as-a-service, drone-as-a-service, NDVI / prescription-map analytics and managed farm-intelligence programmes. Diversified drone or agri-tech companies with an agricultural drone line qualify. NOT core: Tractor-mounted or ground precision-ag equipment makers with no drone; Farm-management software with no drone data; Agrochemical companies (the customers); Drone distributors and dealers of other brands.
